target_customer: Online retailers and consumer brands (early customers included web apps and SaaS companies; later Teleflora, Bonobos, 7 for All Mankind)
problem: Online merchants could not tell which customers were most valuable or at risk of leaving, and lacked data teams to act on order data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for customer analytics and segmentation
product_category: Customer analytics, retention marketing, predictive segmentation

founders.name: Corey Pierson
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. Education and employers not in any opened source.

founders.name: Jon Pospischil
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. A Dealroom snippet attributes a Wharton origin to the idea, not opened, so not recorded as education.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed order-log analysis, customer lifetime value modeling and email integration; standard data engineering with some statistical modeling for a small team in 2011.

defensibility.rationale: Analytics layered on merchants' order data was replicable by email vendors and analytics rivals; stickiness came from integrations with ESPs and ad platforms added later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it early; Amperity acquired it in 2019 to add predictive analytics to its customer data platform and rebranded the product as Amperity Insights.

market_need_then: Ecommerce retailers had order data but few analysts; TechCrunch coverage in February 2011 framed the pain as telling lapsed buyers from lost ones and keeping customers after paying to acquire them.

identity.voice_and_tone: Early tagline: Google brings you customers, we keep them around. Later mission language about removing the mass from marketing.

branding.brand_signature: Early tagline contrasting acquisition and retention

rebrands.why: Product folded into the acquirer's brand after the acquisition, per TechCrunch coverage seen in search results

brand_strength.rationale: Little evidence of brand pull beyond trade press and named retail customers; name origin and identity not covered by any source found.

outcome_analysis: Custora sold retention analytics to online retailers, raised a 2011 seed and a 6.5 million dollar Series A in 2015 led by Foundation Capital, and grew to about eleven staff on the YC page. It ended in a 2019 acquisition by Amperity with terms undisclosed, a modest exit that looks like a team and product tuck-in rather than a breakout.
